title: Weathering and Erosion
seo_title: Grade 4 Weathering and Erosion Worksheets: Water, Wind, Ice and Plants
standard_text: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind, or vegetation.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on weathering and erosion (NGSS 4-ESS2-1): breaking vs. moving rock, deposition, causes like water, wind, ice, plants and gravity, and erosion investigations with data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Weathering breaks rock. Erosion moves it.
key_sub: Water, wind, ice, plants and gravity change Earth's surface. Deposition drops the pieces in a new place.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Water, ice, wind, plant roots and changing temperatures can weather rock.

Erosion moves the pieces of rock and soil to a new place. Water, wind, ice and gravity cause erosion. Deposition drops the pieces in a new place.

We can test erosion with models: water flows faster down a steeper slope and carries away more soil; more water cuts deeper channels; plant roots hold soil and slow erosion.

Example

Ice splits a rock. Is this weathering or erosion?

The rock breaks.

Nothing is carried away yet.

Answer: weathering

Example

A river carries sand downstream. Is this weathering or erosion?

The sand is moved.

Answer: erosion

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up weathering (breaking) and erosion (moving).
  • Thinking plants cause more erosion. Roots hold soil in place.
  • Thinking erosion happens only in big storms. It also happens slowly every day.

faq.q: What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
faq.a: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Erosion moves those pieces to a new place.
Moving water, wind, ice (glaciers) and gravity carry rock and soil to new places.

faq.q: How do plants help stop erosion?
faq.a: Plant roots hold soil in place, so less soil is washed or blown away.
